Manage multiple customer engagements in parallel, prioritizing effectively and communicating status, risks, and next steps to keep implementations on track.

title: AI Platform Engineer
text:
Company Description
It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.
Join us to put AI to work for people.
Job Description
We build the platform that powers ServiceNow AI Workers: autonomous agents that resolve incidents, complete tasks and learn from every interaction. Our engineers work across retrieval, evaluation, agent memory and learning, runtime infrastructure and customer delivery. The goal is simple: give people AI teammates they can trust, so they can spend their time on the work that matters most.
What you’ll do
Design, build and run core services for the AI Worker platform, including agent runtime, orchestration, tool calling and skill management.
Build retrieval pipelines that ground agents in enterprise knowledge, using hybrid search, embeddings, reranking and the ServiceNow AI Search stack.
Develop memory and learning capabilities so agents improve from past resolutions, knowledge articles and human feedback.
Create evaluation frameworks, including offline benchmarks, LLM-as-judge scoring, ablation studies and production quality monitoring, so we can measure whether agents are actually getting better.
Integrate deeply with the Now Platform through scoped apps, GlideRecord, Flow Designer and platform APIs, and make AI capabilities easy for other teams to consume.
Partner with product, architecture and customer delivery teams to take features from prototype to production with real customers.
Own reliability, latency, cost and observability for the services you build.
Raise the bar through design reviews, code reviews and mentoring.
Qualifications
2 to 4 years of software engineering experience, with at least 2 years building ML, LLM or AI-powered systems in production.
Strong programming skills in Java, JavaScript or Python, and solid understanding of distributed systems and API design.
Hands-on experience with LLM application patterns: prompt design, retrieval-augmented generation, tool or function calling, and agent frameworks.
Experience with vector search, embeddings and information retrieval concepts.
A measurement mindset: you’ve designed evals or experiments and used the results to make decisions.
Clear communication and comfort working with distributed teams across time zones.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Nice to have
ServiceNow platform development experience (scoped apps, AI Search, Flow Designer, Now Assist).
Experience with agent memory, continual learning or feedback-driven improvement loops.
Background in IT service management or enterprise workflow automation.
Contributions to open-source AI tooling or published work on agents, retrieval or evaluation.

title: Graduate Software Engineer, Open Source and Linux, Canonical Ubuntu
text:
We are hiring 2026 and 2027 Graduate Software Engineers into engineering teams around the world. As a global platform company we offer a wide range of software engineering challenges, in both open source products and commercial business systems. We have teams that work in a variety of languages, typically Python, Golang, Rust, C/C++, JavaScript and of course... Bash. We work from the very lowest levels of the Linux system - BIOS and boot loaders, firmware, kernel and drivers, all the way up to desktop applications and containers. We work on tiny devices like the Raspberry Pi and new RISC-V boards, all the way up to supercomputers, clouds and Kubernetes clusters. We work on compilers and toolchains, and we work on security, cryptography, performance and documentation. Some of our teams focus on packaging thousands of pieces of software, others focus on deep contributions to a single body of code.

If you are excited about the potential that open source has for humanity and the enterprise, you have outstanding results in your academic career, and you are excited to contribute to the open source stack, this is the best way to apply to Canonical. We will work with you to identify teams and projects that would be interesting and a good fit for your skills and motivations. The process is highly competitive, it will require effort and excellence to succeed if you apply here.

Most of our engineering teams work from home. We try to align a single team in a single time zone - EMEA (Europe, Middle East and Africa), APAC (Asia Pacific and Indian Ocean), and AMER (North, South and Central Americas). Even though you work from home, we try to ensure you always have colleagues alongside to coach and mentor you, and for the companionship of shared problem solving and pair programming. Larger projects have multiple teams and might span the globe. We work with the open source community and specialize in building teams that work well in the 'fishbowl' of open source engineering. This is full time work, five days a week, often solving hard problems with significant responsibility. We don't generally work weekends and nights and we do enjoy good holidays but we also expect productive and intense engagement Monday to Friday.

We bring all our engineering teams together in person twice a year for a deep 'sprint' with other teams to stimulate discussion and enable a wide range of career development paths. This is a fantastic way to demonstrate and develop your skill in software, learn about a wide range of technologies, make a meaningful impact to open source, and see some very interesting new cities that you might never otherwise get to visit.

If you find the open source stack amazing, and you have been a consistent high-performing student in your school and university, then this will be a challenging and exciting start to your career.

Shaping the roadmap for your product at global sprints every six months

Writing high quality, resilient and performant code, potentially serving millions of demanding daily users

Working towards mastery of key programming languages and Linux system knowledge

Engaging with users and the open source community through code reviews and issue trackers

Responding to customer issues as a priority, develop an understanding of enterprise requirements

Developing skills and awareness of security in software design and implementation

Exceptional academic track record from both high school and university

Undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Business Informatics, Mathematics or another STEM discipline with programming courses

Confidence to get started and deliver high quality code in one of Python, Rust, C/C++, Golang, JavaScript or Java

Experience with Ubuntu or another Linux distribution

title: Software Engineer (Core Java, spring boot, restAPI, microservices development, design patterns)
text:
Company Description

Job Description
Software Engineer (T5) 
We are seeking a Software Engineer with solid technical depth to deliver scalable services and guide junior engineers, working with Java, Spring Boot, Python (NumPy), REST APIs, Flask APIs, and Azure. 
Responsibilities: 
Design and develop maintainable, modular software components in Java, Spring Boot, and Python 
Write optimized, reusable, and scalable code that follows SOLID/equivalent principles 
Build application components applying multi-threading, concurrency models, and asynchronous programming principles 
Design, build, and consume REST APIs with Spring Boot and Flask; build Python/NumPy-based data processing components where applicable 
Solve technical problems considering common practice and procedures; determine appropriate action by analyzing possible solutions and their impact on the function/business 
Provide informal guidance to new and junior team members through code reviews and pairing 
Understand how the team’s work integrates with other closely related teams and account for interdependencies 
Write and execute unit tests using JUnit and Mockito; perform API integration testing 
Implement CI/CD pipelines to build and deploy applications; maintain a high level of quality maturity in pipeline quality gates 
Implement security best practices (input validation, authentication, authorization, OWASP guidelines) 
Deploy and operate applications on Azure Cloud using Docker and Kubernetes 
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define, design, and ship new features 
Troubleshoot and resolve issues in development, test, and production environments 
Explain technical, sometimes complex and dynamic concepts clearly to others
Qualifications
3.5- 6+ years of strong working experience in core technical discipline: Java, Spring Boot, RDBMS, NoSQL 
Solid experience with Python and NumPy for building data-oriented services 
Strong experience with common software design patterns (e.g., Adapter, Strategy, Template Method) 
Strong experience in designing, building, and consuming REST APIs efficiently; experience building and operating Flask APIs 
Good experience using AI-assisted tools in the SDLC 
Experience in code execution best practices (memory footprint, GC) and database query analysis (explain plan, statistics) 
Hands-on experience in messaging and queuing 
Proficiency in JUnit; experience with API integration testing using Postman 
Experience in quality gates and security tools integration in CI/CD processes 
Hands-on experience with Docker, Kubernetes, and Azure Cloud services 
Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail 
Strong communication and teamwork skills 
Familiarity with Agile development methodologies
